drhp.business: Mawana Sugars Limited manufactures sugar and generates power at two complexes in Uttar Pradesh (Mawana Sugars Works and Nanglamal Sugar Complex), and produces industrial alcohol (ethanol) at its Nanglamal Distillery. Sugar is sold in the domestic market while ethanol, produced from B-Heavy and C-Heavy molasses, is supplied to Oil Marketing Companies under the government's ethanol-blending programme.
drhp.end_markets: Domestic sugar market (India)|Ethanol supply to Oil Marketing Companies under the government ethanol-blending mandate
drhp.expansion: No new plant or capacity-addition project with a commissioning/completion timeline is disclosed. Disclosed activity is confined to energy-conservation retrofits at the existing sugar/distillery complexes during FY26: retrofitting the rotor and internals of an 8 MW steam turbine to lower specific steam consumption, replacing the mill's old DC drive with an energy-efficient 750 KW AC-VFD motor, and installing variable-speed mechanical circulators for A-massecuite boiling in 4 batch pans, at a capital cost of Rs 410.25 lacs. risks.note: Top Borer, Early Shoot Borer and Red Rot infestations observed over the last three-four years mainly impact the CO-238 & CO-118 cane varieties, which occupy the major portion of the Company's cane area; mitigation relies on integrated pest management and phasing out CO-238 over coming years.
risks.risk: Cane pest/disease infestation concentrated in dominant cane varieties

risks.note: Rapid urbanisation and industrial expansion in Western Uttar Pradesh is reducing the cultivable agricultural land available for cane cultivation, a structural threat to feedstock availability.
risks.risk: Shrinking cane-growing land in the command area

risks.note: The Company's expected sugar selling-price range for FY27 explicitly hinges on there being no revision in Minimum Support Price (MSP), ethanol-blending policy, or export policy - realisations are largely outside management's control.
risks.risk: Government policy dependence for sugar realisations

risks.note: World sugar prices are driven by crude oil (sugar/ethanol parity), the war in West Asian countries, and the global sugar demand-supply balance, exposing the Company's export/parity economics to factors outside its control.

Per the SEBI (LODR) significant-changes disclosure, Operating Profit Margin fell from 6.88% to 4.91% and Net Profit Margin from 4.94% to 2.35% year-on-year, while Return on Net Worth dropped from 15.19% to 7.00%, indicating margin and earnings pressure during the year.

The government may amend the Code of Social Security, 2020, requiring higher gratuity/benefit payments to employees, which would directly increase the present value of the Company's defined benefit obligation.
risks.risk: Legislative risk on employee benefit obligations
